001.4: 1. purpose, scope and applicability 1.1 purpose. this policy sets out the types of leave available to employees of the company, the entitlement to each type of leave, the manner of accrual, carry-forward and encashment, and the procedure for applying for and sanctioning leave. it is intended to allow employees adequate rest and time for personal and family needs while ensuring continuity of service to the company's clients. 1.2 scope. this policy applies to every employee in grades l1 to l8 working at the company's offices in bengaluru, pune, hyderabad, chennai and noida, and to employees working from home or at a client location in india. it does not apply to: (a) consultants, retainers and persons engaged through a manpower agency, whose leave is governed by their contract; (b) interns and apprentices, whose leave is governed by their letter of engagement; and (c) employees on an international assignment, whose leave is governed by the assignment letter and the law of the host country, save that earned leave continues to accrue under this policy. 1.3 effective date and supersession. this policy is effective from 1 april 2025 and supersedes version 4.1. leave balances standing to the credit of an employee on 31 march 2025 are carried forward subject to the accumulation limits in table 1. 1.4 relationship with other policies. the employee handbook (ntl/hr/pol/002) contains a summary of this policy for convenience. in the event of any inconsistency between this policy and the employee handbook or any other policy of the company on a matter relating to leave, including leave encashment, this policy shall prevail. attendance regularisation is governed by the attendance, hybrid work and overtime policy (ntl/hr/pol/006), and notice periods by the separation and exit policy (ntl/hr/pol/008). 1.5 applicable law. this policy is subject to applicable law. notwithstanding anything contained in this policy, where any statute, including the maternity benefit act, 1961, the shops and establishments legislation of the state in which the employee is based, or the national and festival holidays legislation of that state, provides a benefit more favourable to the employee than this policy, the statutory benefit shall prevail to the extent of the inconsistency. 1.6 amendment circulars. the company may amend this policy by issuing an amendment circular in the series hr/cir, approved by the chief people officer. a circular prevails over the clause it amends from the effective date stated in the circular. circulars are reproduced at the end of this policy and form part of it; the body of the policy is not re-issued until the next version. 1.7 interpretation. headings are for convenience only. where a question of interpretation arises, the decision of the head, hr operations, in consultation with the legal department where required, shall be final, subject to applicable law. 2. definitions in this policy, unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms have the meanings given below. words in the singular include the plural and vice versa. 2.1 "basic salary" means the monthly basic pay of an employee as stated in the employee's current compensation letter, excluding all allowances, variable pay, reimbursements and perquisites. 2.2 "calendar day" means any day of the year, including weekly offs and holidays. 2.3 "company" means nexora technologies limited and includes its offices and delivery centres in india. 2.4 "confirmed employee" means an employee whose probation has been completed and who has received a written confirmation of service through the npp. 2.5 "continuous service" means uninterrupted service with the company, including periods of paid leave, maternity leave and authorised absence, but excluding any period of leave without pay exceeding 30 calendar days in aggregate in a leave year and any period of unauthorised absence. ||
001.5: 2.6 "employee" means a person on the permanent or fixed-term rolls of the company in grades l1 to l8, and includes a probationer. 2.7 "hr business partner" means the member of the hr function assigned to the business unit to which the employee belongs, as shown on the employee's npp profile. 2.8 "immediate family" means the employee's spouse, children (including adopted children and stepchildren), parents and legal guardian. for the purposes of this policy, immediate family does not include parents-in-law, siblings, grandparents or any other relative, unless a clause of this policy expressly provides otherwise. 2.9 "leave without pay" (lwp) means absence from duty sanctioned by the company without salary or allowances for the period of absence. 2.10 "leave year" means the period from 1 april of a year to 31 march of the following year. 2.11 "npp" means the nexora people portal, the company's human resources information system, through which leave is applied for, approved and recorded. 2.12 "probationer" means an employee serving the period of probation stated in the offer letter, which is ordinarily six months for grades l1 to l3 and three months for grades l4 to l8. 2.13 "reporting manager" means the person to whom the employee reports administratively, as recorded on the npp. 2.14 "working day" means a day from monday to friday that is not a declared holiday for the employee's base location. a saturday or sunday is not a working day even where the employee's project team or client works on that day under a roster. 3. general principles 3.1 leave is not a matter of right. leave cannot be claimed as a matter of right. sanction of leave is subject to the exigencies of work, and the reporting manager may refuse, defer or curtail leave, recording the reason on the npp. leave shall not ordinarily be refused where the employee would otherwise lose a balance that lapses at the end of the leave year. 3.2 credit of leave. casual leave and sick leave are credited in full on 1 april of each leave year. earned leave is credited monthly, in advance, on the first day of each month at one-twelfth of the annual entitlement in table 1. 3.3 proration for joiners. an employee who joins on or before the 15th day of a month receives the earned leave credit for that month; an employee who joins after the 15th day receives credit from the following month. casual leave and sick leave for the joining year are prorated for the number of months remaining in the leave year, including the month of joining, and rounded to the nearest half day. 3.4 sandwich rule. where a single spell of earned leave covers five or more working days, weekly offs and holidays falling within that spell are counted as earned leave. where the spell covers fewer than five working days, intervening weekly offs and holidays are not counted. the sandwich rule does not apply to casual leave, sick leave or any leave under section 6. 3.5 combination of leave. earned leave may be combined with sick leave and with any leave under section 6. casual leave shall not be combined with earned leave or sick leave, whether by prefixing or suffixing, as provided in clause 5.2. 3.6 minimum unit of leave. casual leave and sick leave may be taken in units of half a day. earned leave shall be taken in units of not less than one full day. 3.7 leave during probation. a probationer accrues earned leave from the date of joining but may avail it only after completing three months of service, save with the approval of the hr business partner in an emergency. casual leave and sick leave are available to a probationer as credited under clause 3.3. ||

001.7: 5. casual leave and sick leave 5.1 casual leave. casual leave (cl) is intended for unforeseen personal needs. not more than three days of cl may be taken at a time. cl is not encashed and lapses on 31 march. 5.2 no combination with earned leave. cl shall not be prefixed or suffixed to el or sick leave. where an employee applies for cl immediately before or after el, the entire spell shall be treated as el and debited accordingly. 5.3 sick leave. sick leave (sl) is available for the employee's own illness or injury. unused sl is carried forward up to a maximum of 24 days and is not encashed at any time. 5.4 medical certificate. sl of more than two consecutive working days shall be supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner, uploaded on the npp within three working days of resuming duty. sl of more than seven consecutive calendar days shall additionally be supported by a certificate of fitness to resume duty. 5.5 exhaustion of sick leave. where sl is exhausted, the absence is debited to el and thereafter treated as leave without pay. cl shall not be used to cover sickness beyond three days. 5.6 special sick leave for hospitalisation. a confirmed employee who is hospitalised for more than seven consecutive calendar days and has exhausted sl may be granted special sick leave on full pay of up to 30 calendar days, once during service, on the recommendation of the hr business partner and the approval of the head, hr operations. hospital discharge papers shall be submitted. 6. maternity, adoption and paternity leave 6.1 general. leave under this section is in addition to the leave in table 1, is not debited from any leave balance and is not subject to the sandwich rule. maternity leave is paid at full salary, comprising basic salary and all fixed allowances; an employee covered by the employees' state insurance scheme receives the maternity benefit from the esi corporation, and the company pays only the difference, if any. 6.2 maternity leave. 6.2.1 a woman employee who has actually worked for the company for not less than eighty days in the twelve months immediately preceding her expected date of delivery is entitled to maternity leave. 6.2.2 maternity leave is 26 weeks, of which not more than eight weeks may precede the expected date of delivery. for a woman employee who has two or more surviving children, maternity leave is 12 weeks, of which not more than six weeks may precede the expected date of delivery. 6.2.3 a probationer shall be eligible for maternity leave of 12 weeks only, and any further absence may be granted as leave without pay at the discretion of the hr business partner. 6.2.4 in the case of miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy, the employee is entitled to leave of six weeks immediately following the day of the miscarriage or termination, on production of a medical certificate. 6.2.5 after maternity leave, the employee may, by mutual agreement with the reporting manager, work from home where the nature of work permits, in accordance with the attendance, hybrid work and overtime policy (ntl/hr/pol/006). creche facilities are described in the employee handbook (ntl/hr/pol/002). 6.3 adoption leave. a woman employee who legally adopts a child below the age of three months, or who is a commissioning mother, is entitled to 12 weeks of leave from the date the child is handed over to her. the adoption order or the relevant medical documents shall be submitted on the npp. 6.4 paternity leave. 6.4.1 a male employee is entitled to paternity leave of 5 working days on the birth of his child or on legally adopting a child below one year of age, to be availed within three months of the date of birth or adoption. paternity leave is available for up to two children during service. 6.4.2 paternity leave shall be taken in a single spell and may be combined with el. ||

returning from leave under this section shall be restored to the same or an equivalent role and grade. the period of leave shall not be counted against the employee in the performance review, and the rating shall be based on the period actually worked. 7. special leave 7.1 bereavement leave. on the death of a member of the employee's immediate family, the employee is entitled to bereavement leave of 3 working days, to be availed within seven calendar days of the death. for the death of any other relative, the employee may apply for cl or el. 7.2 marriage leave. a confirmed employee is entitled to marriage leave of 3 working days once during service, on the occasion of the employee's own marriage, to be availed within one month of the date of marriage and ordinarily combined with el. 7.3 compensatory off. an employee in grades l1 to l4 who is required by the reporting manager, with prior approval recorded on the npp, to work for a full day on a weekly off or declared holiday is entitled to one day of compensatory off. compensatory off shall be availed within 60 calendar days, failing which it lapses, and it is not encashed. employees in grades l5 to l8 are not eligible for compensatory off. overtime payments, where applicable, are governed by the attendance, hybrid work and overtime policy (ntl/hr/pol/006). 7.4 voting. every employee who is entitled to vote in an location is outside that constituency, the employee may apply for up to one additional day of cl or el for travel. 7.5 examination leave. an employee in grades l1 to l5 enrolled in a company-sponsored certification or degree programme may be granted examination leave of up to 5 working days in a leave year, on submission of the examination schedule. 7.6 leave in a natural calamity. where the company declares a natural calamity or civil emergency affecting a location, employees at that location who are unable to work from home may be granted special leave of up to 5 working days, as notified by the head, hr operations. 7.7 court attendance. attendance at a court or tribunal as a witness on behalf of the company is treated as duty. attendance in a personal matter shall be covered by cl or el. 8. leave without pay and sabbatical 8.1 leave without pay. leave without pay may be sanctioned only where the employee has no balance of the relevant leave. lwp of up to 30 calendar days in a leave year may be approved by the reporting manager and the hr business partner; lwp beyond 30 calendar days requires the approval of the chief people officer. 8.1.1 no el accrues for any month in which the employee is on lwp for more than ten calendar days. 8.1.2 lwp exceeding 30 calendar days in aggregate in a leave year does not count as continuous service. 8.2 unauthorised absence. absence without sanctioned leave is treated as lwp and may lead to disciplinary action under the code of conduct and ethics (ntl/hr/pol/004). absence without intimation for eight or more consecutive working days is dealt with under the absconding procedure in the separation and exit policy (ntl/hr/pol/008). 8.3 sabbatical. an employee in grade l5 and above who has completed five years of continuous service may apply for an unpaid sabbatical of three to six months for higher education, research, care of a family member or a personal pursuit of a similar nature. ||
001.9: 8.3.1 a sabbatical may be availed once in every five years of continuous service, and requires the approval of the reporting manager, the business unit head and the chief people officer. 8.3.2 an employee takes el from thursday to the following tuesday. the spell covers four working days (thursday, friday, monday and tuesday), which is fewer than five, so the intervening saturday and sunday are not counted and four days of el are debited. if the same employee takes el from thursday to the following wednesday, the spell covers five working days, so the saturday and sunday are counted and seven days of el are debited under clause 3.4. d.2 how is leave prorated for a new joiner? 003.4: 1. policy statement 1.1 commitment. the company is committed to a workplace free from sexual harassment, where every person is treated with dignity. sexual harassment is a violation of the fundamental rights to equality and to life with dignity, and is also misconduct under the code of conduct and ethics (ntl/hr/pol/004). the company has zero tolerance for sexual harassment and for retaliation against anyone who raises a concern. 1.2 legal framework. this policy is framed in accordance with the sexual harassment of women at workplace (prevention, prohibition and redressal) act, 2013 and the rules made under it. where this policy is silent or inconsistent with the act or the rules, the act and the rules prevail. 1.3 what this policy does. this policy explains what sexual harassment is, how the internal committee is constituted, how a complaint is made and inquired into, the timelines at each stage, the relief available during an inquiry, the action that follows, and the protection given to complainants and witnesses. 2. scope 2.1 who is protected. this policy protects every aggrieved woman, whether she is an employee, a consultant, a trainee, an intern, a visitor, a candidate for interview, or an employee of a client, vendor or contractor, who is subjected to sexual harassment at a workplace of the company or by an employee. 2.2 protection limited to women. the complaint and inquiry procedure under this policy is available to women, as provided in the act. complaints of harassment by or against persons of any gender that are not within the act are dealt with under the grievance procedure described in the employee handbook (ntl/hr/pol/002) and the code of conduct and ethics (ntl/hr/pol/004). 2.3 who may be a respondent. a complaint may be made against any employee, irrespective of grade, including a member of the senior leadership. where the respondent is not an employee, for example an employee of a client or a vendor, the internal committee receives the complaint and the company takes up the matter with the respondent's employer, and supports the complainant in any process of that employer or of the local committee. 2.4 where the policy applies. this policy applies at every workplace as defined in clause 3.10, at all locations of the company in india, whether the conduct occurs during or outside working hours. 3. definitions in this policy, the following terms have the meanings given below. terms not defined here have the meanings given in the act. 3.1 "act" means the sexual harassment of women at workplace (prevention, prohibition and redressal) act, 2013, and includes the rules made under it. 3.2 "aggrieved woman" means a woman of any age, whether employed or not, who alleges that she has been subjected to any act of sexual harassment at a workplace. 3.3 "complainant" means the aggrieved woman who makes a complaint, or the person who makes a complaint on her behalf under clause 6.4. 3.4 a demand or request for sexual favours; making sexually coloured remarks; showing pornography; or any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature. it also includes the following circumstances when they occur in relation to or are connected with such conduct: an implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in employment; an implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment; an implied or explicit threat about present or future employment status; interference with work or creating an intimidating, offensive or hostile work environment; and humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety. 3.10 "workplace" means any place visited by an employee arising out of or during the course of employment, and includes: every office of the company; a client's premises; any place of training, conference, off-site or team event, whether or not organised by the company; transport provided by the company or used for travel on work; hotels and other places of stay during business travel; the employee's home or any other place when used for work; and any virtual space in which work-related interaction occurs, including video calls, chat tools, e-mail, and messaging applications or groups used by colleagues, whether on a company or a personal device and whether during or outside working hours. 4. understanding sexual harassment 4.1 the test is the impact. whether conduct is sexual harassment is judged by whether it was unwelcome to the recipient, not by the intention of the person engaging in it. conduct may be sexual harassment even if it happened once, even if the recipient did not object at the time, and even if others present did not find it offensive. 4.2 examples. examples of conduct that may amount to sexual harassment include: (a) touching, patting, pinching or brushing against a person, or standing unnecessarily close, where this is unwelcome; (b) comments or jokes about a person's body, appearance, clothing, sexual life or sexual orientation, or sexual innuendo; (c) repeated requests for dates or personal meetings after the person has shown disinterest; (d) sending or displaying sexually explicit messages, images, memes, videos or links, including in chat groups; (e) staring, leering, whistling or making sexual gestures; (f) suggesting that a rating, promotion, allocation or extension of contract depends on a personal or sexual relationship; and (g) following, repeatedly calling or messaging a person, or contacting a person on social media, in a manner that is unwelcome. 4.3 what is not sexual harassment. legitimate feedback on performance, allocation of work, or a decision under a company policy is not sexual harassment unless it is connected with conduct of a sexual nature. a consensual relationship between adults is not sexual harassment, but a relationship within a reporting line must be declared under the code of conduct and ethics (ntl/hr/pol/004), and conduct that was once welcome can become unwelcome. 5. internal committee 5.1 constitution. the company has constituted an internal committee at each of its locations, in writing, in accordance with section 4 of the act. each internal committee consists of: (a) a presiding officer, who is a woman employed at a senior level at the location; 004.4: 1. introduction 1.1 purpose. this code sets out the standards of conduct that the company expects of every employee. it explains how to recognise and handle conflicts of interest, gifts, confidential information and other ethical questions, how to raise concerns, and what happens when the code is breached. the code cannot anticipate every situation; where it is silent, employees are expected to act in a way they would be comfortable seeing reported publicly. 1.2 application. this code applies to every employee at every location, including when working from home, at a client site or while travelling, and in personal conduct that affects the company's reputation or business relationships. consultants, contractors and vendors are bound by the supplier code of conduct, which reflects the principles of this code. 1.3 relationship with law and other policies. where applicable law imposes a stricter requirement than this code, the law applies. the policy on prevention of sexual harassment (posh) (ntl/hr/pol/003) governs complaints of sexual harassment, and the it, information security and acceptable use policy (ntl/hr/pol/009) governs information security; this code summarises their requirements for convenience. 1.4 responsibility for the code. the chief ethics officer is responsible for the interpretation of this code, maintains the conflict of interest and gift registers, and reports to the audit committee of the board every quarter on concerns raised and their outcome. 2. definitions 2.1 "business associate" means any client, prospective client, vendor, supplier, subcontractor, consultant, agent or partner of the company, and any of their employees or representatives. 2.2 "conflict of interest" means a situation in which an employee's personal interest, or the interest of a relative, interferes or could reasonably appear to interfere with the employee's duty to act in the best interest of the company. 2.3 "designated person" means an employee who, by reason of role, is likely to have access to unpublished price sensitive information, namely: every employee in grade l8; every employee in grades l6 and l7 in the finance, legal, company secretarial, investor relations and strategy functions; the executive assistants of employees in grade l8; and any other employee notified in writing by the company secretary. an employee who is not a designated person is nonetheless bound by clause 8.2. 2.4 "gift" means anything of value given or received in connection with the company's business, including goods, cash, gift cards and vouchers, discounts not available to the public, loans, services, hospitality, entertainment, travel, accommodation and offers of employment. 2.5 "government official" means any officer or employee of a government, ministry, department, regulator, court, public sector undertaking or government-owned company, any political party or candidate, and any person acting in an official capacity for any of them. 2.6 "relative" means the employee's spouse, parents, children, siblings, the spouses of the employee's children and siblings, and the employee's parents-in-law, and includes any person who lives in the employee's household. this definition applies only to this code and is wider than the definition of immediate family used in the leave policy (ntl/hr/pol/001). 2.7 "trading window" means the period during which designated persons may trade in the company's securities, as described in clause 8.4. 2.8 "unpublished price sensitive information" (upsi) means any information relating to the company or its securities that is not generally available and that, on becoming generally available, is likely to materially affect the price of the securities, including financial results, dividends, changes in capital structure, mergers, acquisitions, disposals, the award or loss of a major contract, and changes in key managerial personnel. 2.9 "whistleblower" means any person who makes a disclosure in good faith under section 13. ||
004.5: 3. our standards 3.1 integrity. employees are honest in all dealings, do not misrepresent facts to clients, colleagues or authorities, and correct errors promptly when they discover them. department before acting. 3.3 managers' additional responsibilities. managers lead by example, ensure that their teams understand this code, create an environment in which concerns can be raised situations that create a conflict of interest. where a conflict of interest cannot be avoided, it is disclosed before the employee takes any decision or action connected with it, and the employee withdraws from that decision unless the ethics office directs otherwise. 4.2 declarations. every employee makes a conflict of interest declaration on the npp on joining and each year by 31 may, and business partner within 15 days. the company then changes the reporting line or responsibilities, without adverse effect on the junior party. 4.5 financial interests. an employee declares any 006.4: 1. purpose, scope and applicable law 1.1 purpose. this policy sets out the working hours of the company, how attendance is recorded, the rules for hybrid work, shifts and on-call support, the payment of overtime, and the transport and safety arrangements for employees who work early or late. 1.2 scope. this policy applies to every employee in grades l1 to l8. leave is governed by the leave policy (ntl/hr/pol/001). where an employee is deployed at a client site, the client's working hours apply where the company has agreed to them, but the limits and payments in this policy continue to apply. 1.3 applicable law. working hours, rest intervals, overtime and the employment of women at night are regulated by the shops and establishments legislation of each state, listed in the leave policy (ntl/hr/pol/001). notwithstanding anything in this policy, where the law of the state in which the employee works provides a limit or a payment more favourable to the employee, the law prevails. in particular, the shops and establishments legislation of the states in which the company operates requires overtime to be paid at twice the ordinary rate of wages, and that rate applies wherever it exceeds the rate in this policy. 2. definitions 2.1 "base location" means the office of the company to which the employee is attached, as recorded on the npp. 2.2 "core hours" means 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on a working day, in the time zone of the base location, during which every employee on the general shift is expected to be available. 2.3 "hybrid work" means an arrangement under which an employee works on some working days from the base location and on others from home, as approved under section 5. 2.4 "night shift" means any shift that ends after 10:00 p.m. or begins before 6:00 a.m. 2.5 "ordinary rate of wages" means the employee's monthly basic salary and allowances forming part of annual fixed pay, excluding variable pay, bonus and overtime payments, divided by 26 for a daily rate and further divided by 8 for an hourly rate. 2.6 "overtime" means work performed at the direction of the reporting manager in excess of nine hours in a day or 48 hours in a week, excluding the rest interval. 2.7 "remote work day" means a working day on which the employee works from home under an approved hybrid work arrangement. 2.8 "working day" has the meaning given in the leave policy (ntl/hr/pol/001), namely a day from monday to friday that is not a declared holiday for the base location. 3. working hours 3.1 standard workday. the standard workday on the general shift is nine hours, including a rest interval of one hour, on each working day, giving about 45 hours of presence and 40 hours of work in a week. within this, an employee may choose the start time between 8:00 a.m. and 11:00 a.m., provided the core hours are covered. 3.2 statutory limits. no employee is required to work more than nine hours in a day or 48 hours in a week, excluding overtime permitted under section 9, or to work for more than five hours continuously without a rest interval of at least half an hour. the spread-over of a workday, including rest intervals, does not exceed the limit prescribed by the law of the state. 3.3 weekly off. saturday and sunday are weekly offs for the general shift. an employee on a shift roster that includes a saturday or sunday receives two other days as weekly offs in the same week, recorded on the roster. 3.4 workload. reporting managers plan work so that employees are not routinely required to work beyond the standard workday. sustained long hours are reviewed by the hr business partner, who may require additional staffing or a change in the plan. ||
006.5: 4. recording attendance 4.1 how attendance is recorded. on days worked at an office, attendance is recorded by the identity card at the entry gates; entry and exit times are transferred to the 007.4: 1. purpose and scope 1.1 purpose. this policy sets out how business travel is approved and booked, the class of travel, hotel and daily allowances to which employees are entitled by grade, and how expenses are claimed and reimbursed. it aims to ensure that employees travel safely and in reasonable comfort, and that the company's money is spent prudently. 1.2 scope. this policy covers domestic and international business travel, local conveyance on company business, and other business expenses such as client entertainment approved under the code of conduct and ethics (ntl/hr/pol/004). relocation on transfer is governed by the employee handbook (ntl/hr/pol/002), and assignments abroad of more than 90 days by the assignment letter. 1.3 client-billable travel. where travel is billable to a client, the client's travel policy applies if it is more restrictive than this policy and the company has agreed to it. the project manager informs the employee of any such restriction before the travel is booked. 2. definitions 2.1 "base location" means the office to which the employee is attached, as recorded on the npp. 2.2 "business travel" means travel away from the base location on the company's business, approved on the npp before the journey, and includes travel to a client site, another company office, a training programme or a conference. 2.3 "metro city" means, for the purposes of this policy only, mumbai, delhi and the national capital region (including noida, gurugram, ghaziabad and faridabad), bengaluru, chennai, hyderabad, kolkata and pune. all other cities in india are non-metro cities for hotel limits. this definition does not apply to the income tax exemption for house rent allowance, for which the compensation and benefits policy (ntl/hr/pol/005) uses a different list. 2.4 "per diem" means the fixed daily allowance paid for each day of business travel to cover meals, laundry, tips and incidental expenses, without the need to produce bills. 2.5 "travel desk" means the team in finance operations, together with the company's appointed travel agency, that books tickets, hotels and transfers for business travel. 3. approval and booking 3.1 travel request. every business travel is requested on the npp, stating the purpose, dates, destination and cost centre, and approved before any booking is made. domestic travel is approved by the reporting manager. international travel is approved by the reporting manager and the business unit head. travel billable to a client also requires the client's approval where the contract so provides. 3.2 booking through the travel desk. tickets, hotels and airport transfers are booked by the travel desk on the basis of the approved request. domestic travel is requested at least seven days, and international travel at least 21 days, before the date of travel, so that economical fares can be obtained. urgent travel at shorter notice is permitted when the reason is recorded on the request. 3.3 lowest logical fare. the travel desk books the lowest available fare on a direct or reasonably timed route within the class of travel entitled. an employee who asks for a particular airline or time for personal convenience, where it costs more than the lowest logical fare by more than rs. 2,000, bears the difference, unless the reporting manager approves it on the request. 3.4 self-booking. an employee may book travel personally only where the travel desk cannot be reached, such as outside its hours for an urgent trip, and must book within the entitlement at the lowest logical fare. the reason is recorded on the claim. 3.5 changes and cancellations. changes and cancellations are made through the travel desk as early as possible. cancellation charges arising from a business reason are borne by the company. charges arising from a personal reason are borne by the employee unless the reporting manager waives them, for example for a medical emergency. 008.4: 1. purpose, scope and precedence 1.1 purpose. this policy sets out how employment with the company ends, the notice periods that apply, the exit process and clearances, the full and final 009.4: 1. purpose, scope and responsibilities 1.1 purpose. the company holds information entrusted to it by clients, employees and partners. this policy sets the rules for using the company's information technology, for protecting information and personal data, and for reporting incidents, so that the company meets its obligations under client contracts and applicable law and protects the people whose data it holds. 1.2 scope. this policy applies to every employee, consultant and contractor who uses a company device, a company or client system, or a byod device for work, at any location, including at home, at a client site and while travelling. 1.3 client requirements. where a client contract or the client's security policy imposes stricter requirements than this policy for a project, the stricter requirements apply to that project. the project manager communicates them at onboarding, and they are recorded on the project's security plan. 1.4 responsibilities. the chief information security officer (ciso) owns this policy and the security programme. the it service desk provides devices, access and first-line support. the security operations centre monitors systems and responds to incidents. the data protection officer oversees compliance with data protection law. every employee is responsible for following this policy and for reporting incidents promptly. 2. definitions 2.1 "byod device" means a mobile phone, tablet or computer owned by an employee and approved under section 7 for access to company e-mail, collaboration tools or systems. 2.2 "client data" means any information, including personal data, provided by or on behalf of a client, or created for a client under a contract, including source code, documents, test data and system credentials. 2.3 "data principal" means the individual to whom personal data relates, including an employee, a candidate, or a customer of a client. 2.4 "information asset" means any information, in any form, and any device, system, application or account on which information is stored or processed, that is owned by or entrusted to the company. 2.5 "multi-factor authentication" (mfa) means the verification of identity by two or more independent factors, such as a password and a code generated on a registered device. 2.6 "personal data" means any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data, as defined in the digital personal data protection act, 2023. 2.7 "personal data breach" means any unauthorised processing of personal data or accidental disclosure, acquisition, sharing, use, alteration, destruction or loss of access to personal data that compromises its confidentiality, integrity or availability. 2.8 "security incident" means any event that compromises or may compromise the confidentiality, integrity or availability of an information asset, including a personal data breach, malware infection, phishing compromise, loss or theft of a device, or unauthorised access. 2.9 "security operations centre" (soc) means the company's team that monitors systems 24 hours a day and responds to security incidents, reachable at itsd@nexora.example or the security hotline 1800-000-0000 (extension 6). 3. information classification 3.1 classification levels. every information asset is classified by its owner at one of four levels, and handled according to table 1. documents carry their classification in the header or footer; where no classification is marked, the information is treated as internal. ||
